about: Board-level KiCad redraws from jotego/jtcores (GPL-3.0), imported by tools/import_jtcores.py. One entry per board; `dir` is the project directory in jtcores at `commit`, `machine` the site machine it belongs to and `machines` any others that run on the same board. The custom chips jtcores draws from the inside are under `chips` (see `chips_about`). Projects in jtcores that are neither are listed under `skipped` with the reason.

boards.name: Kyukyoku Tiger PCB
boards.note: Kyukyoku Tiger is the Japanese release of Twin Cobra; jtcores' ktiger core runs both from this board.

boards.name: Wild West C.O.W.-Boys of Moo Mesa PCB
boards.note: jtcores carries a second copy of this redraw under cores/xmen/sch/moomesa; the one in the moo core is used here.

boards.name: Rally Bike PCB
boards.note: jtcores has no core for this board yet, only the schematic; the game is named on its own sheets.

boards.name: Sly Spy PCB
boards.note: Sly Spy is the US title of Secret Agent; MAME's parent set is secretag.

chips_about: Custom chips jtcores redraws from the inside -- cell by cell off a die photo, or part by part for the 052535 hybrid -- imported by tools/import_custom_chips.py and published as /chip/<slug>. `markings` are what the part is called on a board drawing or in MAME's notes, and are how the boards and layouts that carry it are found; `summary` says what the chip does and is read off the drawing's own notes and sheet names; `conflicts` are places the drawing disagrees with itself, logged rather than corrected.

chips.name: Konami 007779
chips.summary: The tilemap address generator. It holds the scroll registers for both tilemap layers -- horizontal and vertical scroll for each, flip, and a CPU-control enable, at the register addresses the drawing gives -- and switches the video RAM address between the main CPU, the sub CPU and the two tilemaps, by the output-control table on its Outputs sheet.

chips.name: Konami 007780
chips.summary: The tilemap DRAM controller. A three-bit counter steps it through eight pixel clocks -- two fetching tilemap 1, two fetching tilemap 2, two idle and two for a CPU read or write -- and it drives the tile DRAM's row and column addresses and its read and write strobes.

chips.name: Konami 007781
chips.summary: The tilemap pixel shifter. For each of the two tilemaps it latches eight four-bit pixels at a time, with the palette code fetched eight pixel clocks earlier, and shifts them out with fine horizontal scroll and flip applied.

chips.name: Konami 007782
chips.summary: The timing chip. It divides the 18.432 MHz clock (CCLK at 9.216 MHz, CLK2 at 6.144 MHz by the drawing's notes), runs the horizontal and vertical counters, makes sync and blanking, and generates the DMA and data-acknowledge signals.

chips.name: Konami 007783
chips.summary: The sprite addressing chip. It generates the object RAM addresses for reading sprite data and writing it back; the drawing maps that RAM as 0000-17E7h unprocessed data and 1800-1BFFh processed.

chips.name: Konami 007784
chips.summary: The sprite data parser. Fed the unparsed object table, it adds the scroll registers to each sprite's position, sets the sprite-enable bit only when the result is in range, and writes a parsed table back to RAM. It can also fill the table with zeros to clear it.

chips.name: Konami 007785
chips.summary: The sprite-to-tile translator. It scans the parsed object table -- code, palette, position and attributes -- and turns each sprite into the character addresses and colour codes of the tiles it is made of, which the 007786 copies into the frame buffers.
conflicts: Two of the drawing's notes call this chip the 007786: "The 007786 scans for valid object data" and "The 007786 uses an OKI 79V000 gate cell array with 3289 unit cells". Its title block and symbol say 007785, it is drawn in the OKI MSM70V000 cells the 007781's 3289-cell array is drawn in, and the 007786's own drawing gives that chip a different array (OKI 74V000, 2400 cells), so both notes are taken to describe this chip.

chips.name: Konami 007786
chips.summary: The sprite frame buffer controller. With SEL low it generates the frame-buffer addresses; with SEL high it handles the sprite character data being written in. It also refreshes the frame-buffer DRAM. A Twin 16 board carries three.

chips.name: Konami 007787
chips.summary: The pixel multiplexer. It selects between the frame buffers' pixel outputs, switched by the horizontal pixel count (H1F, H2F) and P256VD by the equations on the drawing, and passes the result on in pixel order.
conflicts: The drawing's note on the gate array reads "The 007786 uses an Fujitsu C540AVB, MB674149U CMOS gate array with 549 gates". It is on this chip's only sheet, which is drawn in Fujitsu AV cells, and the 007786's own drawing gives that chip an OKI array, so the note is taken to describe the 007787.

chips.name: Konami 052535
chips.summary: A five-bit video DAC, one each for red, green and blue -- a hybrid in a ceramic SIP-9, by MAME's notes on The Simpsons. Five data inputs and a blanking input drive a resistor ladder into an NPN output transistor. Its author says the resistor values, found by simulating the circuit and measuring a real part, are close rather than certain.

chips.name: Capcom DL-010D-103
chips.summary: The video timing chip: horizontal and vertical counters, sync and blanking. HSEL selects a 384- or a 512-clock line, 256 or 384 pixels of it visible, by the drawing's own table. The die is an NEC uPD65000-series gate array, which agrees with MAME's notes on Last Duel calling the same marking an NEC custom.

chips.name: Capcom DL-020F-108U
chips.summary: The CPU's address decoder. From the Z80's address and control lines it makes the memory selects ($0000-7FFF, $8000-BFFF, $C000-C7FF, $C800-CFFF, $D000-DFFF and $E000-FFFF by its table), the read and write strobes for the I/O ports, and the ROM bank select.

chips.name: Capcom DL-050-115V
chips.summary: The sprite line buffer. It takes sprite data, position and palette in, writes the pixels into even- and odd-line buffers held in RAM on the chip, and shifts the colour out for display, with horizontal flip and an option to invert the colour outputs. Pang's board has it marked BUNRAKU DL-050-115V, by MAME's notes.
